        Hand-picked AI tools

        Chat & Assistants

        • ChatGPT: OpenAI's everyday assistant: chat, files, pictures, voice and agents that browse and act for you.
        • Claude: Anthropic's assistant, careful writing, long documents and serious coding help.
        • Gemini: Google's assistant, plugged into Search, Gmail, Docs and your Android phone.
        • Grok: xAI's assistant, with what people are posting on X right now in reach.
        • Microsoft Copilot: Microsoft's assistant across Windows, Edge and the Office apps.
        • Meta AI: Meta's assistant inside WhatsApp, Instagram and Messenger, or on its own.
        • Le Chat: Mistral's fast European assistant, with web search, documents and code.
        • DeepSeek: Free chat with DeepSeek's open-weight reasoning models.
        • Qwen Chat: Alibaba's Qwen models to chat with, text, images, video and code.
        • Kimi: Moonshot AI's assistant, known for reading very long documents and agentic work.
        • Poe: One app for most of the big models, plus bots other people have built on them.
        • Character.AI: Chat and role-play with characters, made by you or by the community.
        • Pi: A warm, conversational companion that's good at talking things through.
        • HuggingChat: Chat with the best open models, free, in Hugging Face's own app.
        • Duck.ai: DuckDuckGo's private AI chat: popular models, conversations kept anonymous.
        • Brave Leo: The assistant built into the Brave browser, private by design.
        • Replika: An AI companion that remembers you and chats like a friend.
        • Z.ai: Chat with Zhipu's GLM models, strong at coding and agentic tasks.
        • Monica: An all-in-one assistant in your browser: chat, summarise pages, write and translate.
        • Merlin: A browser extension that brings top models to any page you're reading.
        • Sider: A sidebar assistant for reading, writing and chatting with several models at once.
        • TypingMind: A polished chat app for your own API keys, bought once, used with any model.
        • Msty: A desktop app to chat with local and online models side by side.

        Research & Search

        • Perplexity: Ask anything, get an answer written from the web with every source cited.
        • NotebookLM: Turns your own documents into a notebook you can question, and a podcast about them.
        • Elicit: Finds the papers on a question and pulls the findings out into a table.
        • Consensus: Answers questions from peer-reviewed studies, and shows how far they agree.
        • Semantic Scholar: Ai2's search engine for scientific papers, with one-line summaries of each.
        • Kagi Assistant: The ad-free search engine's assistant: the big models, grounded in Kagi's results.
        • You.com: Search and research agents that write up what they find, with citations.
        • SciSpace: Reads papers with you: explains passages, compares studies and drafts literature reviews.
        • Scite: Shows how a paper has been cited, supported, disputed or just mentioned.
        • ResearchRabbit: Maps the papers around the ones you care about, and keeps you posted on new ones.
        • Connected Papers: A visual graph of the papers related to any one you start from.
        • Undermind: A research agent that reads hundreds of papers to find the ones that really answer you.
        • Liner: An AI search engine for students and researchers, with trustworthy sources.
        • Felo: Multilingual AI search that can turn its answers into slides and mind maps.
        • ChatPDF: Upload a PDF and ask it questions; answers point back to the page.
        • Humata: Ask questions across long documents and get cited, page-linked answers.
        • Julius AI: A data analyst you talk to: upload spreadsheets, get charts and answers.
        • Wolfram|Alpha: Computes answers, maths, science, data, rather than searching for them.

        Coding

        • Claude Code: An agent that works in your terminal and editor: reads the codebase, makes changes, runs the tests.
        • Cursor: A code editor built around AI, autocomplete that predicts edits, and agents that take tasks.
        • GitHub Copilot: Code suggestions, chat and a coding agent inside your editor and on GitHub.
        • Codex: OpenAI's coding agent, in the cloud, the terminal or your IDE, that ships pull requests.
        • Windsurf: An AI-native editor whose agent follows along with what you're doing.
        • Google Antigravity: Google's agent-first IDE: hand agents whole tasks and review what they did.
        • Gemini CLI: Google's open-source coding agent for the terminal, with a generous free tier.
        • Jules: Google's asynchronous coding agent: give it an issue, get back a pull request.
        • Replit: Describe an app and its agent builds, hosts and deploys it in the browser.
        • Lovable: Full-stack web apps from a conversation, with a real database behind them.
        • Bolt: Prompt, run, edit and deploy full-stack apps without leaving the browser tab.
        • v0: Vercel's builder for polished React interfaces and apps from a prompt or a sketch.
        • Cline: An open-source coding agent for VS Code that asks before every step it takes.
        • Aider: Pair-programming in the terminal that commits each change to git as it goes.
        • Zed: A very fast open-source editor with AI and agents built in.
        • Warp: A terminal where agents can run commands, fix errors and write code with you.
        • Kiro: AWS's agentic IDE that plans from specs before it writes the code.
        • JetBrains AI: AI chat, completion and the Junie coding agent inside JetBrains IDEs.
        • Gemini Code Assist: Google's coding assistant for VS Code and JetBrains, free for individuals.
        • Amp: Sourcegraph's agentic coding tool for the editor and the terminal.
        • Augment Code: An AI coding agent that understands very large codebases.
        • Tabnine: Private code completion and chat that can run on your own servers.
        • Qodo: AI that writes tests and reviews code for quality before it ships.
        • CodeRabbit: Line-by-line AI reviews on every pull request.
        • Greptile: Code review that understands your whole repository, not just the diff.
        • Devin: Cognition's autonomous software engineer, working in its own sandbox.
        • Factory: 'Droids' that take coding tasks from ticket to pull request.
        • OpenHands: An open-source platform for AI software agents that code like a developer.
        • Roo Code: An open-source team of AI coding agents inside VS Code.
        • Kilo Code: An open-source coding agent for VS Code and JetBrains, with hundreds of models.
        • Continue: Open-source assistants and checks for your editor and your pull requests.
        • Mintlify: Beautiful developer documentation, kept up to date with AI.
        • Pieces: Remembers what you worked on across tools so your AI has the context.
        • Firebase Studio: Google's cloud workspace for building full-stack apps with Gemini.
        • Base44: Working apps, with login and a database, from a description.
        • Rork: Native mobile apps from a prompt, ready to test on your phone.
        • GitHub Spark: Small full-stack apps from plain English, hosted for you on GitHub.

        • Google Colab: Python notebooks in the browser, with free GPUs to start.
        • Lightning AI: Cloud studios to code, train and serve models on GPUs.
        • Unstructured: Turns PDFs, slides and messy documents into data ready for LLMs.
        • Jina AI: Embeddings, rerankers and a reader that turns web pages into clean text.
        • Voyage AI: High-quality embeddings and rerankers for retrieval.
        • Tavily: A search API made for AI agents and RAG.
        • Browserbase: Headless browsers in the cloud for AI agents to drive.
        • E2B: Secure cloud sandboxes where AI agents can run code.
        • GPT4All: Run language models privately on your own computer.
        • AnythingLLM: A private all-in-one AI app: chat with documents, agents, any model.
        • LocalAI: A drop-in, self-hosted replacement for the OpenAI API.
        • Smithery: A registry of MCP servers to plug tools into your AI apps.
